head: 82e6692038269b91dcf7aeed577d7b6649beca1c
summary:
I reviewed SL-110 as committed in 82e6692 against f764c34 and found no defects. The product change does what the design says.
- FolderTreeNode reads ScanStore.NotListed once per row. OnDiskText, SizeText, ShareText and ShareShown all go through one HasFigures gate. The Note arm returns TopLevelRowText.NotReadYet, and it sits before the unreadable words.
- OffersStoppedTree is `Cancelled && TopLevel is not null`.
- ShowOutcome still opens a stopped ending on the list (Q-273) and shows the 'Folder tree' radio button unchecked.
- OnResultsViewChanged swaps the tree and the list only while that button is visible, so the Completed path is unchanged.
- ResetTreeChoice runs before ClearFolderTree, so the stopped store is let go when the next scan starts.
- The store rule holds: BuildFolderTree and ShowStoppedTree take a parameter named `result`. Fitness check: 99 rules hold. Rule 2's regex fires on all 4 of the pre-slice guards and on none of the new code.

What I ran:
- Full suite: 1023/1023 pass.
- Window cases: T-010 passed in 14 s. It stopped at m-mid\ and the store marked 202 entries not listed; the walk read 202, all drawn 'not read yet' with blank figures. Its 3 runs, including the view switch and the rescan release, all passed.
- T-011 passed in 61 s: pressedAt == j-before, m-big cut with NotListed and childCount 0, panel empty.
- T-012 passed in 75 s, which is more than the builder's 61-63 s. Stopped and completed opens of the 100k-child folder were all under 500 ms.
- T-006 passed.
- SL-063 passed 10/10 and SL-100 passed 29/29.
- T-003 fails only on its 'taller window' VOID check (241.9 px against 241.9 px); all five of its opens pass. That matches the builder's declared environmental account.
- I did not run R-004 (it opens real Explorer windows), WindowMutants -Mutant All, the rules harness or RuleCases. For those I rely on the code and the builder's recorded runs.

Each case-matrix test I read builds the shape it is meant to test, and its void rules stop a late or early Stop from passing. Where the code departs from the design without saying so, the change is small and does no harm; those departures are listed under drift. I filed one minor extra finding: the StopTarget census regex in StopTargetTests can be bypassed by a double-quoted or variable target, or by a target set in another script.

Second round: Second lap found one new problem, a minor error-path defect in test fixture code (m2, filed as extra). New-StoppedTreeFixture denies b-listed\denied before most of the T-010 tree is built. If any later step of the build throws, the deny ACE is never undone, and the case folder is left on disk where Remove-Item cannot delete it. Everything else I probed holds.

What I checked on this lap:
- **StopTarget.Matches** against the root forms the hook can produce: drive root `C:\` trimmed to `C:` and rejoined, UNC, a trailing backslash on either side, and case. All match as intended.
- **The spin's double read** (`_currentFolder` then the CurrentFolder getter). A missed raw value is caught on the next pass, and a subtree target matches any later value under it.
- **A click that races the end of the scan.** It would be judged as a FAIL instead of VOID, but every fixture leaves at least 40-60 ms of work after any matching value, so it cannot happen on these cases.
- **FSA_HOOK_VIEWS and CAN_REVEAL parsing** of empty and unknown values. The new hook variables are always removed in Invoke-WithHook's finally, so they cannot leak into the next case.
- **RevealMode's new note/mark fields** cannot throw: the container is never null at that point.
- **The census regex** does not pick up the $HookVariables list line.
- **The corpus reader** handles `seenFull`; ids are unique.
- **WPF radio event order** for tree→Folders, tree→kinds, kinds→tree and ResetTreeChoice: each handler sees a consistent IsChecked and Visibility.
- **OnCanOpenInExplorer's focus fallback** when the tree or list collapses.
- **WindowReport's schema** is untouched.
- **OffersStoppedTree with an empty-root Cancelled result** is offered but harmless.
- **The on-demand build throwing** from the Checked handler is the Q-071 shape that was deferred by decision (m3), not new.

Also noted, but no current case depends on it: the corpus bounded_by's claim that 'the hook compares the same form' as LongPath does not hold for `\\?\`-prefixed launch roots. The hook uses Path.GetFullPath, which keeps the prefix that ToDisplay strips. No case launches that way.

findings.claim: The StopTarget census that guards against the M1 shape reads only single-quoted assignments in WindowCases.ps1. EveryStopTargetAWindowCaseNamesIsASubtreeOrAnAllowedExactFolder matches `FSA_HOOK_TREE_STOP\s*=\s*'([^']+)'`, so three kinds of future case would slip past it: an exact target with a short successor written in double quotes (`FSA_HOOK_TREE_STOP = "m-mid\d05"`), one passed through a variable, or one set in another script (HookCases.ps1, WindowMutants.ps1). That case would then fail the way M1 described, with 'ended-first' refusals after a minute of fixture building, instead of failing in the default suite. Every target in the tree today is single-quoted and in WindowCases.ps1, so nothing is missed now.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/StopTargetTests.cs:78; corpus bounded_by in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/StopTargetCorpus.json claims 'a new FSA_HOOK_TREE_STOP in a case that names one exact folder ... fails the census'
findings.fix: Change the regex to accept either quote (`FSA_HOOK_TREE_STOP\s*=\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]`). Fail the census when any `FSA_HOOK_TREE_STOP` occurrence in tests/window/*.ps1 is not a literal assignment it can read.

findings.claim: New-StoppedTreeFixture denies the listing of b-listed\denied at line 6431, then builds most of the tree: 5,000 c-prefix folders, about 4,000 m-mid files and 250 p-folder files. It returns $denied only on its last line. If any of that later work throws (an IOException or an AggregateException out of Bulk.Folders, or a full disk), Test-T010's `$denied` is still $null. Its finally then skips Undo-DenyListing, and Remove-CaseFolder's `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` cannot list the denied folder, so it throws from the finally. The real build error is hidden behind the cleanup error, and a folder with a deny-list ACE stays under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-window-cases. A later scan of C:\ or of Temp then counts it as an unreadable code-5 row, which is the scratch-leak shape of #333 and Q-266.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:6429-6432 (Deny-Listing before the bulk build); Test-T010 at :6605 assigns $denied only from the function's return value, and its finally at :6685-6686 undoes the ACE only when $denied is set.
findings.fix: Move `Deny-Listing $denied` to the end of New-StoppedTreeFixture, just before `$denied` is returned. Then a failure while building the tree leaves no ACE behind.

obligations.evidence: I ran T-010 run 1: p00-p04 are the only not-listed rows at depth 1. Each draws note 'not read yet' with blank on-disk, size and share, no bar and no expander, and storeNotListed is true (CheckStoppedRows, WindowCases.ps1:6498-6499).
In my T-010 run, 197 of m-mid's 200 subfolders at depth 2 were not listed, and all of them drew 'not read yet' with no figures (the check at WindowCases.ps1:6500-6501).

The store-marks count comes from StoppedTree.StoreMarks, which reads LastResult.Store by reflection, not the rows. It equals the number of walked not-listed rows (202 = 202 in my run; check at WindowCases.ps1:6482).
In my T-010 run, a-empty and b-listed\empty both have note '', '0 bytes', no expander and storeNotListed false (WindowCases.ps1:6508-6514).
m-mid is listed, has no note, draws 12.0 KB and has an expander (WindowCases.ps1:6517-6519; observed in my run).
b-listed\denied reads 'could not be opened', the panel names it, and the panel names no not-listed path (WindowCases.ps1:6522-6532; observed).

Each depth-1 tree row is compared with its stopped-list top-row: NotRead exactly when the store marks it, and the title is '<name>  (<tree note>)'. The states Done, StoppedPartway and NotRead all appear in the same run (WindowCases.ps1:6535-6547). SL-063 passed 10/10 when I ran it.

VIEWS runs kinds,folders,tree,folders,tree. After the tree, choosing Folders brings back the list with the stopped header, and its 9 titles are byte-identical to before (CheckStoppedViews, WindowCases.ps1:6574-6578; observed). The code path is MainWindow.ShowStoppedList.

I ran T-011: pressedAt == j-before (exact), m-big storeNotListed true, childCount 0, note 'not read yet', blank figures, no bar or expander, empty panel, and the list title is 'm-big  (not read yet)'.

I ran T-012. m-big was listed with 100,000 children and at least 5,000 not-listed rows (the void rule at WindowCases.ps1:6772), and all five opens were under 500 ms. notListedChildren is computed after the timed region in TreeMode.ExpandTimed (line 526), so it does not inflate the timings.
In my T-010 run, the can-reveal line for p04 shows selected and focused, canExecute true, pathOf = root\p04 = storePath, storeNotListed true. PathOf itself is unchanged.

StoppedTreeOfferTests.TheTreeIsOfferedExactlyWhenTheRootsListingCommitted sweeps the Stop over every guarded call, before and during it. It asserts that the empty-store, not-listed-root and offered shapes were each reached (lines 82-85) and that the predicate matches the store each time. It passed in my run of the suite (1023/1023).

In T-010 run 2 (completed), treeChoice is false, kinds then Folders leaves the tree with one item and the same header, and no row is marked or reads 'not read yet'. T-012's completed run has notListedChildren 0. Both observed.

tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StopTarget.cs:31-41 matches subtrees, and the corpus and StopTargetTests run in the default suite, which passed. The cases' targets are m-mid\, j-before, m-big\ and n-slow\. The census misses non-single-quoted spellings (finding m1, extra).

Test-R004 (WindowCases.ps1:6828-6844) puts n-slow, 3,000 subfolders, between the stop target and z-unread, and voids the run unless z-unread reads storeNotListed and 'not read yet'. I did not run R-004 because it opens Explorer; this is from the code and the builder's mutation record.

MainWindow.OnResultsViewChanged returns before the swap unless ShowTreeButton is Visible. T-010 run 2's kinds→folders step passed in my run and shows the finished tree with one item and an unchanged header.

T-011 and T-012 are separate cases with their own fixtures. Measured here: T-010 14 s, T-011 61 s, T-012 75 s (the builder had 61-63 s). All are under 120 s with the app published and the hook already built. T-012's margin is about 45 s, so a cold publish plus hook build makes it the case closest to the limit.
StoppedTree.Spin (lines 132-156) busy-reads _currentFolder through a volatile DynamicMethod, with no sleep in the poll. My T-011 log shows pollMeanNs 19.7 and worstGapMs 7.6.

StoppedTreeHeader leads with 'Not read yet: folders the stop came before.' T-010 shows 109 of 201 characters at 880 px and 48 at the 560 px minimum, and checks that the lead and the word survive the ellipsis (observed).
Same as O-002/O-003: T-010 run 1, observed.
Same as O-013: StoppedTreeOfferTests passed in the suite.
Same as O-005: T-010 run 1, observed.
Same as O-008: T-010 plus SL-063, both run by me.
Same as O-010: T-011, run by me.
Same as O-007: T-010, observed.
Same as O-011: T-012, run by me.

T-012's completed run (WindowCases.ps1:6796-6809): notListedChildren 0, cold open 117.9 ms in my run. T-003's five opens also pass (cold 92.4 ms here). T-003 exits 1 only on its environmental 'taller window' VOID check, which I reproduced.
Same as O-012: T-010 can-reveal on p04, observed.

Test-R004 checks status '' , Exact and Explorer selecting z-unread; an unreadable selection becomes Inconclusive and exits 3, never a pass (WindowCases.ps1:6852-6873). I did not run it because it opens real Explorer windows, so the landing rests on the builder's run.
T-010 run 2, observed. T-001 was not re-run by me.

T-006 passed in my run ('FolderTree is not shown after a stop'). SL-100 passed 29/29 and SL-063 10/10 when I ran them. I did not run L-001 or WindowMutants -Mutant All; those rest on the builder's record.

In T-010 run 3, observed: tree chosen, p04 selected, Release, the stopped store collected twice, after-release shows treeChoice false and foldersChecked true, and the second tree's rows have no 'not read yet'. The code path is MainWindow.ResetTreeChoice then ClearFolderTree.
Run 3 sets FSA_HOOK_SELECT=p04. TreeMode.AfterRelease (lines 623-636) logs the radio buttons and the second store's marks and walks one level. All of it was observed in my run.

StoppedTree.cs:412-468: StoreMarks, NotListedOf, NotListedChildren and StorePathOf are NoInlining, resolve LastResult.Store on each call, and return only values. The run-3 store-released checks were true twice.

The fitness.yaml SL-110 rule-1 entry was edited in place and names the actual headers. ListHeader and StoppedTreeHeader (MainWindow.xaml.cs:407-409, 525-529) build their words from TopLevelRowText.NotReadYet. Fitness check passes.

cases.evidence: T-010 run 1 stops at m-mid\. Its void rule (T010Needs) requires a not-listed row at depth 1 and both listed and unlisted rows under m-mid at depth 2. In my run: p00-p04 at depth 1 and 197 m-mid subfolders at depth 2, each read through the store's mark.

StoppedTreeOfferTests puts 1500 long-named files in the root so a Stop can land inside the root's listing, and sweeps every guarded call k, before and during it. It asserts the empty-store, not-listed-root and offered counts are each greater than 0.
The T-010 fixture has a-empty (depth 1) and b-listed\empty (depth 2), both listed before m-mid. The check needs storeNotListed false and '0 bytes' with no note.
T-010 compares each depth-1 tree row with the same-named stopped-list top-row in the same run (NotRead vs the store mark, and the title vs the tree note). p00-p04 are the 'stop came before' folders.

T-011 voids the run unless pressedAt == root\j-before (the last committed folder, so m-big's 100k listing was in flight) and m-big reads storeNotListed true with childCount 0. In my run it was hit on the first launch.

The T-010 fixture denies b-listed\denied with Deny-Listing. The check requires 'could not be opened' and that the panel names it, beside the unread folders, and that no not-listed path is in the panel.

This row is material:false by design. No real scan can produce an entry that is both NotListed and in Unreadable. StoppedTreeOfferTests (lines 76-77) asserts the disjointness on every swept Stop, but no test builds a session with such an entry, so which Note arm wins is never run. The design accepted that, so I filed no finding.
T-012 stops at m-big\ (the 100k-child folder is listed), voids unless notListedChildren is at least 5,000 (WindowCases.ps1:6772), then opens it 5 times. In my run all opens were under 500 ms.

T-003's 100k-file open runs and all five opens pass (cold 92.4 ms). Its command exits 1 only on the environmental VOID check, so as named it cannot read green on this PC. T-012's completed run (notListedChildren 0, opens under 500 ms) covers the shape, which the builder declared.
T-010 sets CAN_REVEAL=p04, a not-listed depth-1 row. The hook selects and focuses it, then asks OpenInExplorer.CanExecute and PathOf. Observed canExecute true and path root\p04.

Code read, not run: R-004's fixture puts n-slow, 3,000 subfolders, between the stop and z-unread, and voids unless z-unread's row reads storeNotListed true and 'not read yet'. It then does a real menu reveal and reads the selection through Shell.Application.
T-010 run 2 is a completed scan with VIEWS=kinds,folders. It checks that treeChoice is false and that the tree is visible with 1 item and the same header after going back to Folders (observed).
T-006 passed in my run (stopped, nobody picks the tree, FolderTree not shown). CheckStoppedRun in the new cases also asserts list shown, tree hidden and choice offered. SL-100 passed 29/29.
T-010 run 3: Stop at m-mid\, tree chosen, p04 selected, then FSA_HOOK_RELEASE to a small tree that completes. after-release and the second tree's rows were checked (observed).

drift: RevealMode.FindInTreeItem (tests/window/FsaWindowHook/RevealMode.cs:815-826) gained an exact direct-child pass before its depth-first search. That changes tree-target navigation for every reveal case (R-001, R-002, R-003), though the design said reveal mode runs 'tree:' targets 'exactly as after a completed scan'. It was not declared, and R-001 to R-003 were not re-run after it. I traced their current targets and found no name collision that would change which row is picked.

ResetTreeChoice (MainWindow.xaml.cs:534-540) checks Folders only when the tree was the choice. If File kinds was picked, it stays across the scan. The design said 'StartScan checks ShowFoldersButton'. The built behaviour keeps SL-046's rule that the kinds choice outlasts a scan; not declared.

Smaller undeclared fixture and retry changes: R-004's c-prefix has 3,000 folders, not the design's 5,000. T-010 run 1 retries a void run up to 3 launches, not 'retried once'. Neither affects what is proved.
T-012 took 75 s in my run, against the builder's 61-63 s. That is still under the 120 s case limit, but with a cold publish and hook build it is the new case closest to the limit (O-018).

The StopTargetCorpus.json bounded_by says a `\\?\` launch root is excluded 'because the hook compares the same form' as LongPath.NormalizeRoot. StoppedTree.Spin actually uses Path.GetFullPath(_launchPath).TrimEnd('\\'), which keeps the `\\?\` prefix that LongPath.ToDisplay strips from CurrentFolder. A future case launched that way would never match, and every run would go void. No current case launches that way.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-110/*.json (engine-owned stage records, not code; only index.json and code-review files are mine to read)
